findings.claim: Coinbase's Q3 2026 Form 10-Q reports $325.766 million recognized customer derivatives collateral at September 30, 2026: BTC $322.341 million and ETH $3.425 million. XRP is not listed in that recognized derivatives-collateral table.
Coinbase's broader crypto-assets-held-as-collateral balance was $1.2995 billion at September 30, 2026, but the filing does not allocate that total to XRP or to Deribit.

Coinbase reports $2.804112 billion of unrecognized customer crypto collateral in lending arrangements, but no token-level breakdown; it must not be counted as recognized derivatives collateral or as XRP.
Coinbase states customer assets are not used as collateral for loans, margin, rehypothecation or similar activities without customer consent.

Deribit's October 14 custody policy lists Coinbase Custody Trust Company in the cold-wallet provider set and Coinbase Institutional UK Limited in the warm-wallet provider set; it still describes Coinbase Bermuda Limited as to be added after September 2026.

The CFTC/Deribit XRP collateral pathway was legally and technically plausible by late 2026, but the Q3 Coinbase filing does not show recognized XRP derivatives collateral through September 30. October 1 platform integration and the October 14 custody-policy wording indicate a phased integration; post-integration Q4 usage remains unverified.

It is unknown whether CBBM was added to Deribit's warm-wallet custody stack after October 14, whether CFM's notice and initial three-month restriction were completed, and whether any U.S. customer posted XRP after September 30.

The Q3 recognized derivatives-collateral table contains BTC and ETH only; the current Deribit custody policy still described CBBM as a future addition as of October 14. These facts disconfirm any claim that XRP collateral was already demonstrably live in Coinbase's recognized derivatives collateral by September 30.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Coinbase enables XRP cross collateral for eligible CFM/Deribit customers after the Q3 reporting cutoff and after the CFM-specific three-month initial restriction.
disconfirming: No CFM notice date or post-September XRP balance was found; CBBM was still described as to be added in the October 14 custody policy.
competing_hypotheses.test: Locate the CFM notice/commencement date, later custody-policy revision, customer terms and Q4 collateral reporting.

competing_hypotheses.statement: CFM's recognized derivatives collateral remains primarily BTC and ETH; XRP is eligible at the venue but not enabled or not materially used by CFM customers.
support: Coinbase Q3 10-Q recognized derivatives collateral table lists BTC and ETH only.
disconfirming: The Q3 reporting cutoff precedes the October 1 Deribit integration and later Q4 product rollout.
competing_hypotheses.test: Review Coinbase Q4 10-Q and any subsequent CFM collateral disclosure.

non_equivalences: Coinbase's $1.2995B total crypto collateral is not XRP-specific.
Unrecognized lending collateral is not the same as recognized derivatives collateral.
Corporate assets pledged against borrowings are not customer-posted XRP margin.
Q3 September 30 disclosures predate the October 1 Deribit integration completion.
A custody provider being listed is not evidence of actual XRP held at that custodian.
